messages:

Subject: Novamed MAP kickoff: acceptance anchors and evidence needs

Hi Sofia / Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Attached is our internal view of the evaluation timeline and the draft MAP we pulled together — please see MAP_Draft.xlsx. Goal for this thread: lock the specific acceptance anchors (what counts as "pass"), the minimum evidence we will accept, and the cutover/canary dates so Legal/Procurement can start paperwork.

High level asks from Novamed:
- Functional: >90% accuracy on discharge summary extraction (measured on Novamed test set)
- Safety: no PHI leakage outside VPC during eval; audit trail for every request
- Performance: 95th pctl latency <= 300ms for typical payloads (50–250 tokens)
- Handoff: clear pass/fail gates and a rollback plan for canary cutover

Can you confirm what specific tests you will need from Redwood and what owners (internal + Novamed) will be responsible for each evidence item?

Also looping Legal for timing — we may need a signed MAP before any dedicated capacity is reserved. Dana

Subject: Re: Novamed MAP kickoff: acceptance anchors and evidence needs

Thanks Dana — this is helpful. I reviewed the spreadsheet; below are the acceptance anchors and the minimum acceptance tests Redwood proposes. I attached the smoke test checklist (smoke_tests.md).

Proposed acceptance anchors (short):
- Accuracy: model F1 >= 0.90 on Novamed-labeled discharge set (shadow eval)
- Concordance: embedding similarity A/B concordance >= 0.85 across sample queries
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 300ms on canary hardware + typical batching (50–250 tokens)
- Availability: 99.5% for the dedicated test window (two-week eval)
- Security: SOC2 evidence + ephemeral logs for each test request; no outbound data egress outside VPC

Minimum acceptance tests and owners:
- Functional smoke (owner: Novamed ops) — 100 de-identified cases run through the pipeline, golden labels compared. Evidence: result CSV + test harness logs.
- Throughput & latency (owner: Redwood infra) — 1-hour load window at projected qps, 95th pctl report. Evidence: Grafana export + token-level timing.
- Privacy audit (owner: Novamed security + Redwood security) — verify network flow logs, request traces. Evidence: packet-level summary + KMS audit entries.
- Safety sampling (owner: Redwood product) — 500 random outputs sampled for PHI leakage; manual review doc.

Exit gates (if any one of the following fails, trigger defined response):
- Functional threshold miss by >5% absolute -> stop + triage -> target remediation window 5 business days
- Latency missed by >50ms at 95th pctl -> switch to fallback model variant for canary
- Any demonstrable egress of PHI -> immediate stop and incident escalation

Next steps:
1) Redwood to provide the smoke_tests.md (attached) and sample payloads by EOD Tue (we did).
2) Novamed to confirm owners and sign the MAP (DocuSign link to follow).
3) Technical canary window proposed: Jul 6–9 (two-week staggered ramp to production thereafter).

Let me know gaps or if you want a short call to walk through each test.

— Sofia
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple operational notes from the mutual-action perspective:

- Escalation path: if an acceptance anchor fails during the canary, Novamed ops -> Redwood CS -> Redwood Eng -> Exec on-call. We will document SLAs for triage timelines in the MAP.
- Contractual gate: procurement has requested that the MAP be signed before we allocate dedicated capacity. If Novamed needs Dedicated earlier, we can provision with a 30-day provisional window but that requires Legal okay.
- Acceptance handshake: once evidence is produced for a test, owners have 48 hours to acknowledge and 5 business days to dispute with samples. Absence of dispute = implicit acceptance.

Thanks — adding a few technical details so we have exact test definitions we can automate:

- Functional test harness: Redwood will run the 100-case smoke set (de-identified) through the shadow endpoint; we will return per-case labels + confidence. Pass defined as F1 >= 0.90 and no single class with recall < 0.80. Evidence: CSV (case_id, predicted, label, confidence) + execution log.
- Embedding concordance: for 1k pairs from Novamed reference corpus, mean cosine agreement between Redwood embeddings and Novamed reference vectors must be >= 0.85. We'll provide the runner and the seed used.
- Load profile: typical qps = 5, spike qps = 20. Canary run: 1 hour at typical qps, 1 10-minute spike at 20qps. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency and error rate.
- Canary rollout policy: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic over 48 hours with health checks (error rate < 0.5% and p95 within target). Rollback triggers: error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes or p95 > target + 100ms for >5 minutes.

I'll populate the exact measurement scripts and expected output formats in the MAP spreadsheet (columns for artifact links).

— Karthik
Director, Inference Engineering
